There may be flaw(s) in the implementation of WICKR, but according to cryptographic principles, it is theoretically flawless within its limitations. It cannot provide, for instance, genuine perfect forward secrecy and the attendant plausible deniability concurrent with PFS. It cannot conceal that any two given parties are in communication, even if the actual identities of each party are hidden. Traffic analysis would determine which party is communicating with which given enough surveillance. But ideally, and according to cryptographic principles/discrete logarithm problem/Diffie-Hellman ideals, the content of your communications is absolutely indecipherable to anyone whom either party has not specifically notified.

Honeypots are still a possibility.

Recipient could still screen capture via secondary device without notification.

But assuming you trust recipient to be discrete and minimally trustworthy, and a cryptographic representation of one's identity need not be absolutely concealed, it is - barring discovery of some significant flaw in its implementation - very sound and reliable.

Anonymity is preventing any association to your real identity. I think it is possible but isn't very convenient.

Tails can prevent identifying your real MAC address, browser fingerprint, and other things. Tails also doesn't save anything to your computer so there's no evidence left behind.

Never access any of the accounts, and preferably websites, from your home/work network. Find networks that are miles away from home, either open or learn to crack WPS networks.

You might also consider changing how you write and think about how you structure your sentences (length, number of commas, words used).

You can also look for stories where anonymous members and tor users are caught, see if you can't find out how they got caught. I remember seeing one person using tor that was busted by accessing a compromised server and had scripting enabled, although I couldn't find a source. Noscript isn't installed by default in Tails, last I checked, you should probably install it along with other addons it might not have.

It might be a good idea to use a single anonymous identity per access point, since it would give an idea of your movements and compromise other access points/accounts. It would be better to use services that didn't require logging in.
